findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: getWishDetailsTool, listMyConversationsTool, readConversationTool, openRikmaConversationTool, listRikmaProcessesTool, prepareMissionTool, startProcessTool, attachToProcessTool, prepareSignup · Private data: postConversationMessageTool, openRikmaConversationTool, startProcessTool, prepareSignup · Public sink: setAssistantItemsTool, shareRikmaPreviewTool, postConversationMessageTool, scanProjectDirectionsTool, prepareSignup · Destructive: setAssistantItemsTool, reviseAssistantTool.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: getWishDetailsTool, listMyConversationsTool, readConversationTool, openRikmaConversationTool, listRikmaProcessesTool, prepareMissionTool, startProcessTool, attachToProcessTool, prepareSignup · Private data: postConversationMessageTool, openRikmaConversationTool, startProcessTool, prepareSignup · Public sink: setAssistantItemsTool, shareRikmaPreviewTool, postConversationMessageTool, scanProjectDirectionsTool, prepareSignup · Destructive: setAssistantItemsTool, reviseAssistantTool

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
